paragraphs: State Street Corporation is one of the world's leading providers of financial services to institutional investors, including investment servicing, markets and financing solutions and investment management. Our clients — asset managers and owners, insurance companies, wealth managers, official institutions and central banks — rely on us to deliver solutions that support their business objectives across the investment life cycle. Leveraging our strength and scale, innovation and platforms, and industry expertise, we are an essential partner to our clients. In all aspects of our business, we work toward a singular purpose: to help create better outcomes for the world's investors and the people they serve.

Through our subsidiaries, including our principal banking subsidiary, State Street Bank and Trust Company, referred to as State Street Bank, we operate in more than 100 geographic markets worldwide, providing a broad range of financial products and services to institutional investors globally. As of December 31, 2025, we reported $53.80 trillion in AUC/A and $5.67 trillion in AUM. We had consolidated total assets of $366.05 billion, consolidated total deposits of $274.35 billion, consolidated total shareholders' equity of $27.84 billion and approximately 52,000 employees as of December 31, 2025.

State Street Corporation, referred to as the Parent Company, was organized in 1969 under the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, and is a bank holding company that has elected to be treated as a financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956. The Parent Company is a source of financial and managerial

strength to our subsidiaries. We conduct our business primarily through State Street Bank, which traces its beginnings to 1792, with the founding of our oldest ancestor bank, Union Bank. State Street Bank's current charter was authorized by a special Act of the Massachusetts Legislature in 1891, and its present name was adopted in 1960. State Street Bank operates as a specialized bank, referred to as a trust or custody bank, that services and manages assets on behalf of its institutional clients.

Our corporate headquarters is located at One Congress Street, Boston, Massachusetts 02114 (telephone (617) 786-3000). For purposes of this Form 10-K, unless the context requires otherwise, references to "State Street," "we," "us," "our" or similar terms mean State Street Corporation and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis.

On the "Filings & reports" tab of our website at investors.statestreet.com, we make available, free of charge, all reports we electronically file with, or furnish to, the SEC including our Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and Current Reports on Form 8-K, as well as any amendments to those reports, as soon as reasonably practicable after those documents have been filed with, or furnished to, the SEC. These documents are also accessible on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov. We have included the website addresses of State Street (including references to investors.statestreet.com) and the SEC in this report as inactive textual references only. Information on those websites (or any other) is not incorporated by reference in this Form 10-K.

We have Corporate Governance Guidelines, as well as written charters for the Examining and Audit Committee, the Executive Committee, the Human Resources Committee, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, the Risk Committee and the Technology and Operations Committee of our Board of Directors, or Board, and a Code of Ethics for Senior Financial Officers, a Standard of Conduct for Directors and a Standard of Conduct for our employees. Each of these documents is accessible on the "Corporate governance" tab of our website at investors.statestreet.com.

Our operations are organized into two lines of business: Investment Servicing and Investment Management, which are defined based on products and services provided.

Our Investment Servicing line of business provides a broad range of investment servicing and market and financing solutions to institutional clients, including mutual funds, collective investment funds and other investment pools, corporate and public retirement plans, insurance companies, wealth managers, investment managers, foundations and endowments worldwide.

Through State Street Investment Services and State Street Markets, we offer a full range of back-, middle- and front-office solutions, including custody, accounting and fund administration services for traditional and alternative assets, as well as multi-asset class investments; recordkeeping, client reporting and investment book of record, transaction management, loans, cash, derivatives and collateral services; investor services operations outsourcing; performance, risk and compliance analytics; financial data management to support institutional investors; foreign exchange, brokerage and other trading services; securities finance, including prime services products; and deposit and short-term investment facilities.

Together with our back- and middle-office services, CRD's front- and middle-office technology offerings form the foundation of State Street Alpha. Our State Street Alpha platform combines portfolio management, trading and execution, analytics and compliance tools, along with advanced data aggregation and integration with other industry platforms and providers. paragraphs: In the normal course of our business activities, we are exposed to a variety of risks. The following is a discussion of material risk factors applicable to us. Additional information about our risk management framework is included under "Risk Management" in Management's Discussion and Analysis in this Form 10-K. Additional risks beyond those described in our Management's Discussion and Analysis or in the following discussion may apply to our activities or operations as currently conducted, or as we may conduct them in the future, or in the markets in which we operate or may in the future operate.

The markets in which we operate across all facets of our business are both highly competitive and global. These markets are changing as a result of financial and technological innovation and new and evolving laws and regulations applicable to financial services institutions. For example, the adoption and implementation of evolving and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and distributed ledger technology, and related regulatory frameworks, have the potential to disrupt materially the activities of the financial services industry, the operation of financial markets, processes, infrastructure and service providers, including State Street, and the servicing and other requirements of financial services clients, including our clients. Market changes, macroeconomic developments and other factors, whether as a result of financial, technological or regulatory changes or otherwise, cannot always be anticipated, and may adversely affect the demand for, and profitability of, the products and services that we offer, potentially materially. In addition, new market entrants and competitors may address or influence changes in the markets more rapidly than we do, may have materially greater resources to invest in infrastructure, technology and product development than we do, or may provide clients with a more attractive or cost-efficient offering of products and services, adversely affecting our business. All of these effects may occur, regardless of our response to these financial, technological, regulatory or other changes, including our own investment in innovation, product development, business process optimization and regulatory compliance. Our efforts to develop and

market new products, particularly in the "Fintech" sector including through State Street Alpha and broader digital asset-related initiatives or in attractive areas of focus such as wealth servicing and alternative investment management, may position us in new markets with pre-existing or less regulated competitors with strong market position. We have also experienced, and anticipate that we will continue to experience, significant pricing pressure in many of our core businesses, particularly our custodial and investment management services. This pricing pressure has and may continue to impact our revenue growth and operating margins and may limit the positive impact of new client demand and growth in AUC/A or AUM. Many of our businesses compete with other domestic and international banks and financial services companies, such as custody banks, investment advisors, broker/dealers, outsourcing companies, information providers, data analytics and processing companies. Further consolidation within the financial services industry could also pose challenges to us in the markets we serve, including potentially increased downward pricing pressure across our businesses.

Some of our competitors, including our competitors in core services, have substantially greater capital resources than we do, are not subject to as stringent capital or other regulatory requirements as we are, or may not be as constrained as we are by these requirements due to the relative size of our balance sheet. In some of our businesses, we are service providers to significant competitors. These competitors are in some instances significant clients, and the retention of these clients involves additional risks, such as the avoidance of actual or perceived conflicts of interest and the maintenance of high levels of service quality and intra-company confidentiality. Our relationships with other businesses, including competitors, necessarily involve the sharing of confidential information, and we cannot be certain, notwithstanding the existence of confidentiality obligations on the part of those other businesses, that our information will not be used to the competitive advantage of others. The ability of a competitor to offer comparable or improved products or services at a lower price would likely negatively affect our ability to maintain or increase our profitability. Many of our core services are subject to contracts that have relatively short terms or may be terminated by our client after a short notice period. In addition, pricing pressures as a result of the activities of competitors, client pricing reviews, and rebids, as well as the introduction of new products, may result in a reduction in the prices we can charge for our products and services.

management, and in our financial results, due to the significant size of our relationship with many of our institutional clients, and are also subject to significant pricing pressure due to trends in the market for custodial services and the considerable market influence exerted by those clients.

Our clients include institutional investors, such as mutual funds, collective investment funds, UCITS, hedge funds and other investment pools, corporate and public retirement plans, insurance companies, official institutions, foundations, endowments and investment managers. In both our investment servicing and investment management businesses, we endeavor to attract institutional investors controlling large and diverse pools of assets, as those clients typically have the opportunity to benefit from the full range of our expertise and service offerings. Due to the large pools of assets controlled by these clients, the loss or gain of one client, or even a portion of the assets controlled by one client, or a client's decision to in-source certain services that we provide, could have a significant effect on our AUC/A or our AUM, as applicable, in the relevant period. Loss of all or a portion of the servicing of a client's assets can occur for a variety of reasons. Our AUM or AUC/A are also affected by decisions by institutional owners to favor or disfavor certain investment instruments or categories. Similarly, if one or more clients change the asset class in which a significant portion of assets are invested (e.g., by shifting investments from emerging markets to the United States), those changes could have a significant effect on our results of operations in the relevant period, as our fee rates often change based on the type of asset classes we are servicing or managing. As our fee revenue is significantly impacted by our levels of AUC/A and AUM, changes in levels of different asset classes could have a corresponding significant effect on our results of operations in the relevant period. Large institutional clients also, by their nature, are often able to exert considerable market influence, and this, combined with strong competitive forces in the markets for our services, has resulted in, and may continue to result in, significant pressure to reduce the fees we charge for our services in both our investment servicing and investment management lines of business. Our historical focus on the segments of the market for investor services represented by very large asset managers and asset owners causes us to be particularly impacted by this industry trend. Many of these large clients are also under competitive and regulatory pressures that are driving them to manage the expenses that they and their investment products incur more aggressively, which in turn exacerbates their pressures on our fees. paragraphs: State Street Corporation 是全球主要的金融服務供應商之一，為機構投資者提供相關服務，包括投資服務、市場與融資解決方案以及投資管理。我們的客戶 —— 資產管理機構與所有者、保險公司、財富管理機構、官方機構與中央銀行 —— 依賴我們提供解決方案，以支持他們在投資生命週期中的業務目標。透過我們的優勢與規模、創新與平台，以及產業專業知識，我們是客戶不可或缺的夥伴。在所有業務方面，我們致力於一個單一目標：協助創造更好的投資者與他們所服務人羣的結果。

透過我們的子公司，包括我們的主要銀行子公司 State Street Bank and Trust Company，簡稱 State Street Bank，我們在全球超過 100 個地理市場運作，為全球機構投資者提供廣泛的金融產品與服務。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們報告的 AUC/A 為 53.80 兆美元，AUM 為 5.67 兆美元。我們的合併總資產為 366.05 兆美元，合併總存款為 274.35 兆美元，合併總股東權益為 27.84 兆美元，並約有 52,000 名員工，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。
State Street Corporation，簡稱為 Parent Company，於 1969 年根據馬薩諸塞州法律設立，並為一家銀行控股公司，已選擇被視為根據 1956 年銀行控股公司法的金融控股公司。Parent Company 是我們子公司的財務與管理強項來源。

我們主要透過 State Street Bank 進行業務運作，State Street Bank 的起源可追溯至 1792 年，當時創立了我們最古老的祖先銀行 Union Bank。State Street Bank 的現行章程於 1891 年經馬薩諸塞州立法機構特別法案授權，並於 1960 年採用現名稱。State Street Bank 作為一家專門銀行運作，簡稱為信託或保管銀行，為其機構客戶管理與服務資產。
本公司總部位於馬薩諸塞州波士頓康克爾街1號（電話 (617) 786-3000）。就本Form 10-K而言，除非上下文另有要求，否則提及「State Street」、「我們」、「我們」、「我們」或類似詞彙時，均指State Street Corporation及其子公司合併後的狀況。

本公司業務運作分為兩大業務線：投資服務及投資管理，此分類係根據所提供的產品及服務來界定。
我們的投資服務業務線為機構客戶提供廣泛的投資服務及市場與融資解決方案，這些機構客戶包括共同基金、集資投資基金及其他投資池、企業與公共退休計畫、保險公司、資產管理公司、財富管理公司、投資管理公司、以及全球各地的基金會與大學基金。

透過 State Street Investment Services 及 State Street Markets，我們提供完整的後臺、中臺及前臺解決方案，包括傳統與另類資產的保管、會計及基金管理服務；記錄保管、客戶報告及投資帳戶記錄、交易管理、貸款、現金、衍生性商品及擔保服務；投資者服務運作委外；績效、風險及合規分析；支持機構投資者的財務資料管理；外匯、經紀及其它交易服務；證券融資，包括主營服務產品；以及存款及短期投資設施。

與我們的後臺及中臺服務共同組成 State Street Alpha 的基礎，是 CRD 的前臺及中臺科技解決方案。我們的 State Street Alpha 平台結合了投資組合管理、交易與執行、分析與合規工具，以及與其他產業平台及供應商的先進資料整合與聚合。CRD 的科技解決方案包括 Charles River Investment Management Solution，這是一項前臺科技解決方案，可自動化並簡化跨資產類別的機構投資流程，從投資組合管理與風險分析，到交易及交易後結算，並整合合規與管理資料；Charles River for Private Markets，這是一項針對投資於私募信貸、私募股權、不動產、基礎建設及基金的機構的投資管理解決方案；以及 Charles River Wealth Management Solution，這項解決方案提供投資組合管理、交易合規及管理人/

本公司業務活動使我們面臨利率風險。
paragraphs: 本公司在日常營運活動中，面臨多種風險。以下為適用於本公司的重大風險因素討論。有關我們風險管理架構的額外資訊，請參閱本10-K表格中「風險管理」部分的「管理層討論與分析」。除了本「管理層討論與分析」或以下討論中所描述的風險外，可能仍存在其他風險，這些風險可能影響我們目前或未來的營運活動，或我們目前或未來在營運的市場。

我們在所有業務面向所營運的市場，皆為高度競爭且全球性。這些市場因財務與科技創新，以及適用於金融服務機構的新法律與規範而持續變化。例如，人工智慧與分散式帳本技術等新興與演進中的科技，以及相關的監管架構的採用與實踐，可能對金融服務產業的活動、金融市場的運作、流程、基礎設施與服務提供者（包括State Street）以及金融服務客戶的相關服務與需求（包括我們的客戶）造成重大影響。市場變化、總體經濟發展及其他因素，無論是因財務、科技或監管變動或其他原因，皆無法總是預測，且可能對我們所提供的產品與服務的銷售需求與獲利產生不利影響，可能達到重大程度。此外，新進市場參與者與競爭對手可能比我們更快應對或影響市場變化，可能擁有比我們更大量的資源用於基礎設施、科技與產品開發，或可能提供客戶更具吸引力或成本效益的產品與服務，對我們的業務造成不利影響。所有這些影響，無論我們如何應對這些財務、科技、監管或其他變動，包括我們自身的創新投資、產品開發、業務流程優化與監管合規，都可能發生。我們努力開發與

推廣新產品，特別是在「金融科技」領域，包括透過State Street Alpha與更廣泛的數位資產相關計畫，或在財富管理與另類投資管理等有吸引力的業務領域，可能使我們進入具有預設或較少監管的競爭對手的新市場，這些競爭對手在市場上擁有強大的地位。我們也已經經歷，並預期將持續經歷，在許多核心業務中的顯著價格壓力，特別是在我們的保管與投資管理服務。這種價格壓力已並可能持續影響我們的收入成長與營運毛利，並可能限制新客戶需求與AUC/A或AUM成長的正面影響。我們的許多業務與其他國內外銀行與金融服務公司競爭，例如保管銀行、投資顧問、經紀商/經紀人、委外公司、資訊提供者、資料分析與處理公司。金融服務產業進一步的併購，也可能對我們在服務的市場造成挑戰，包括可能增加我們業務中的向下價格壓力。

一些競爭對手，包括我們在核心服務中的競爭對手，擁有遠較我們更大的資本資源，並不受我們所受的資本或其他監管要求那麼嚴格，或可能因我們資產負債表相對規模而較不受這些要求的束縛。在一些我們的業務中，我們是重要競爭對手的服務提供者。這些競爭對手在某些情況下是重要客戶，而保留這些客戶涉及額外的風險，例如避免實際或被視為利益衝突，以及維持高水平的服務品質與公司內部機密性。我們與其他企業，包括競爭對手的關係，必然涉及機密資訊的分享，我們無法確定，儘管這些其他企業有機密義務，我們的資訊不會被用於他人的競爭優勢。競爭對手提供可比或更優質的產品或服務，且價格更低的能力，將可能對我們維持或提高獲利能力產生負面影響。我們許多核心服務受到合約的約束，這些合約的期限較短，或客戶在短通知期後可能終止。此外，因競爭對手的活動、客戶的價格審查與重新招標，以及新產品的推出，可能導致我們能收取的產品與服務價格減少。
管理層，以及在我們的財務結果中，由於我們與許多機構客戶的關係規模龐大，也受到市場保管服務趨勢以及這些客戶的市場影響力所造成的顯著價格壓力。

我們的客戶包括機構投資者，例如共同基金、集體投資基金、UCITS、對沖基金及其他投資池、企業與公共退休計畫、保險公司、官方機構、財團、基金會與投資管理公司。在我們的投資服務與投資管理業務中，我們努力吸引控制大量且多樣化資產池的機構投資者，因為這些客戶通常有機會從我們的專業知識與服務方案中受益。由於這些客戶控制的資產池規模龐大，失去或獲得一個客戶，甚至一個客戶所控制的資產中的一部分，或客戶決定將我們提供的某些服務內化，都可能對我們在相關期間的AUC/A或AUM產生重大影響。失去客戶資產的服務，可能因多種原因而發生。我們的AUM或AUC/A也受到機構所有者對特定投資工具或類別的偏好或不偏好決策的影響。同樣地，如果一個或多個客戶改變其資產類別中資產的配置（例如，將投資從新興市場轉移到美國），這些變化可能對我們在相關期間的營運結果產生重大影響，因為我們的費用率通常根據我們服務或管理的資產類別類型而變化。由於我們的費用收入大幅受到AUC/A與AUM水平的影響，不同資產類別水平的變化可能對我們在相關期間的營運結果產生相應的重大影響。大型機構客戶也因其本質，往往能對市場產生相當大的影響力，這種影響力，加上我們服務市場中的強大競爭力，已導致並可能繼續導致我們在投資服務與投資管理業務中，對我們服務的費用收取產生顯著的壓縮壓力。我們歷來對投資者服務市場中非常大型的資產管理人與資產所有者所代表的業務領域的專注，使我們特別受到此產業趨勢的影響。許多這些大型客戶也受到競爭與監管壓力，促使他們更積極地管理他們及其投資產品所產生的費用，這進一步加劇了他們對我們費用的壓力。因此，我們從任何特定客戶或任何特定客戶委託業務中產生的服務費用，可能低於我們預期
